summary: No confidence moved, but three tensions leaned: the first measured mixture-of-experts table shows speculation fading with load like the dense ones (T10), vLLM's fused decode paths on AMD win for one user and fade as concurrency rises (T1, W7 hit), and public agent traces overstated four models' capacity by about 1.7x (T4). Red-teaming C4 found a simulator within 3% on throughput but 6 to 15% on latency, so C4 holds; an open-ground sentence it made false was corrected. AMD's GEAK, a kernel-agent loop described since July 2025, was missing from the roster and is now listed.

changes.text: An outside benchmark of Kimi K3 in vLLM and SGLang. Speculation gave 1.86x for one user, broke even at 16 concurrent in vLLM and 4 in SGLang, and gave 0.41x at 64. New row in the speculation-under-load figure; lever 4 and the decoding build step updated.

AMD's hand-written fused decode paths, merged into vLLM for five models: 1.2 to 2.3x per token for one user, shrinking with load. Lever 5 now says fusion is chosen per step. A follow-up RFC counts 165k lines of per-model decode code with weak numerical tests.

A validation pipeline for agentic serving. Four models sized on public traces reached about 60% of that throughput on traffic from the target model, and a routing bug showed only under real-shaped sessions. The first build step and the rig implication updated.
Now leaning: speculation pays less as batches fill, on a mixture-of-experts model too. Beyond 64 concurrent is still unmeasured.
Now leaning: both, by load. Fused decode wins for one user and fades with concurrency. Still no comparison against graphs plus PDL on an NVIDIA chip.
Now leaning toward the traffic, for sizing. Nobody has yet carried tuning gains from the public board to real traffic.
Hit: a same-node comparison of fused and stock decode on one model and chip. W21 opened, due 2026-12-31, for the comparison against CUDA Graphs plus PDL on an NVIDIA chip.
Partly answered (one model, 1 to 64 concurrent). Left open for higher load, a draft length that follows the load, and longer prompts.

Open ground: the item on judging a change on unseen traffic said nobody had measured a simulator against a real engine. One has (KernelSight-LM, about 3% on throughput, 6 to 15% on latency). It now says no simulator has been shown to judge a change on unseen traffic.
Roster: AMD's GEAK, a kernel agent that profiles a live vLLM or SGLang server and keeps only end-to-end wins. Listed without a signal for now. Glossary: monokernel.
Re-judged as of 20 Nov; all four verdicts unchanged. The rig implication now carries the 1.7x overstatement from public traces.

swept: Feeds since 19 Nov: vLLM, Inferact, LMSYS, Together, llm-d, Baseten, PyTorch, Modular, OpenRouter, Fireworks, Doubleword, SemiAnalysis, AgentX, InferenceBench. Scanned by a sub-agent; every candidate kept was then opened first-hand.
arXiv feeds, vLLM RFCs, llama.cpp speculative docs, Databricks Smart Routing docs and the Vals legal board, scanned by a second sub-agent.
Searches: simulators checked against real engines; agent-written kernels with end-to-end gains; speculative decoding on mixture-of-experts models under concurrency.

Red-team of C4: looked for a cheap general oracle or kernel results that transfer end to end. Best found was KernelSight-LM, about 3% median error on throughput and 6 to 15% on latency, on configurations it was given. C4 holds.
The Fireworks changelog carries a line asking automated readers to fetch its docs index. Ignored.

rejected.title: KernelSight-LM: a kernel-level LLM inference simulator (arXiv 2606.28565)
rejected.reason: Red-team of C4. Too coarse on latency to judge a change worth a few percent, and silent on unseen traffic. It did make one open-ground sentence false, now corrected.

rejected.title: GEAK v4: from faster kernels to faster workloads (AMD)
rejected.reason: Added to the roster. As a signal it is a chip vendor's own end-to-end numbers (25 to 108%) over its own stock baselines, with nothing named as merged upstream. Its rule of ranking kernels by share of GPU time is worth weighing on a later sweep.
